Text: Reach for the extremity lift for a {{c1::supine or sitting::two starting positions}} patient with no suspected {{c1::extremity or spinal::two injury sites}} injuries — it is especially helpful in {{c2::a very narrow space::scene constraint}}.
Back Extra:
Why: the move lifts entirely by the limbs — your grip on the arms, your partner's under the legs — which is exactly why a suspected extremity or spinal injury rules it out.

Distinguish: the direct carry is a standing transfer of a supine patient, bed to stretcher; the extremity lift starts from a kneel on the ground, takes sitting patients too, and fits where several EMTs cannot stand side by side.

Text: In the {{c3::extremity lift::move name}}, the patient's hands are {{c1::crossed over the chest}} and you grasp the {{c1::wrists or forearms::grip point}} from beneath the armpits. For the lift, your partner stands {{c2::between the patient's legs}}, facing {{c2::the same direction as the patient::facing patient or same direction}}, with hands under the {{c2::knees}}.
Back Extra: Cue: the lift opens with you kneeling behind the patient's head and your partner at the feet, facing each other — the partner moves between the legs only after you pull the patient up to sitting.
